name: ExecuteAutomation MCP Database Server
purpose: Query and manage Postgres, SQL Server, and SQLite databases from an AI agent via one MCP server
description: NodeJS MCP database server covering Postgres, SQL Server and SQLite with connection-reference docs, connection-string or named-database setup, and table/query tools. Demonstrated end-to-end in the Execute Automation channel video.
connect_steps: hermes mcp add database-server -- npx -y executeautomation/database-server
Set DB connection env (e.g. MYSQL_HOST, MYSQL_USER, MYSQL_PASSWORD or SQL Server/Postgres connection strings) in config.yaml mcp_servers env block
Restart Hermes and verify: ask the agent to list tables in a connected database
source: youtube:Database MCP Server: Connect Postgres DB, SQL Server and Sqlite

name: MySQL MCP Server
purpose: Run SQL queries and manage MySQL databases directly from natural language
description: Python-based MCP server (pip/uvx installable) that lets an LLM execute SQL against local or remote MySQL. Covered in Rahul Shetty Academy's agent-building video where it powers a registration/login workflow.
connect_steps: hermes mcp add mysql -- uvx mysql-mcp-server
Provide MYSQL_HOST, MYSQL_USER, MYSQL_PASSWORD, MYSQL_DB env keys in config.yaml mcp_servers
Restart and verify: ask the agent to run SHOW TABLES on the target database
source: youtube:Build AI Agent with MCP Servers to Automate - Browser, API, SQL & File Systems

name: Playwright MCP (Microsoft)
purpose: Browser automation and web testing via Playwright's accessibility tree
description: Official Microsoft MCP server exposing browser_navigate, browser_click, browser_snapshot and testing tools. Shown in Rahul Shetty's agent video (npx @playwright/mcp@latest) and GitHub's Copilot CLI tutorial for validating web apps.
connect_steps: hermes mcp add playwright -- npx @playwright/mcp@latest
Optional flags: --headless, --isolated, --viewport-size for controlled runs (config.yaml mcp_servers args)
Restart and verify: ask the agent to open a URL, click an element, and report the page state
source: youtube:Build AI Agent with MCP Servers to Automate - Browser, API, SQL & File Systems

name: Selenium MCP
purpose: Control browsers through Selenium WebDriver for automation and QA
description: Python MCP server wrapping Selenium WebDriver so AI agents can drive real browsers (Chrome/Firefox) with WebDriver primitives. Mentioned as the Selenium alternative to Playwright MCP in Rahul Shetty's browser-automation agent tutorial.
connect_steps: pip install selenium-mcp (requires ChromeDriver/geckodriver on PATH)
hermes mcp add selenium -- uvx selenium-mcp
Restart and verify: ask the agent to open a page and extract page title
source: youtube:Build AI Agent with MCP Servers to Automate - Browser, API, SQL & File Systems

name: Browser MCP (BrowserBase)
purpose: Let the AI drive your own real Chrome browser via extension + local server
description: browsermcp.io MCP server: a Chrome extension connects your everyday browser to a local MCP server, so agents can navigate logged-in sessions, click, type and screenshot. Shown for automated testing and task automation by Elie Steinbock and All About AI (with Cursor).
connect_steps: Install the Browser MCP Chrome extension (browsermcp.io) and pin it
hermes mcp add browsermcp -- npx browsermcp@latest
Open the extension, point it at http://localhost:7788 and connect
Verify: ask the agent to browse a site you are already logged into
source: youtube:Automate your browser with Browser MCP

name: Stagehand MCP (Browserbase)
purpose: Natural-language browser automation framework (act/extract/observe) exposed over MCP
description: Browserbase's Stagehand MCP (@browserbasehq/mcp) brings act(), extract(), and observe() browser actions to MCP clients, with cloud browser or local Chromium support. Linked from Elie Steinbock's browser-automation video resources (stagehand.dev / browserbase.com).
connect_steps: hermes mcp add stagehand -- npx @browserbasehq/mcp
Set BROWSERBASE_API_KEY (and BROWSERBASE_PROJECT_ID) env keys for cloud browsers; omit for local Chromium
Restart and verify: ask the agent to extract data from a page using extract()
source: youtube:Automate your browser with Browser MCP

name: GitHub MCP Server (official)
purpose: Full GitHub API access: repos, issues, PRs, actions, code search, teams
description: GitHub's official open-source MCP server (github/github-mcp-server) connecting AI tools to the GitHub platform with OAuth or PAT auth. Covered by GitHub's own channel, Cloud Champ's VS Code tutorial, and Copilot CLI docs.
connect_steps: Create a GitHub PAT (repo, read:org scopes) or use OAuth
hermes mcp add github -- docker run -i --rm -e GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN ghcr.io/github/github-mcp-server (or remote URL https://api.githubcopilot.com/mcp/)
Restart and verify: ask the agent to list your starred repos sorted by stars
source: youtube:Github MCP Server in VS Code : Everything Explained with Examples [Demo]

name: Docker MCP Gateway
purpose: Run containerized MCP servers from Docker's catalog behind one gateway connection
description: Docker's MCP gateway (docker/mcp-gateway) lets one connection serve many official MCP servers (DuckDuckGo, Fetch, GitHub, Notion, etc.) from a catalog, with custom catalogs supported. NetworkChuck's tutorial builds a custom catalog and connects Cursor/Claude to it.
connect_steps: Install Docker Desktop and start the engine
hermes mcp add docker-mcp -- npx -y docker-mcp
Add servers from the Docker MCP catalog (e.g. duckduckgo, fetch) or point to a custom catalog YAML
Restart and verify: ask the agent to use one of the catalog tools
source: youtube:you need to learn MCP RIGHT NOW!! (Model Context Protocol)

name: Power Automate Flow Agent MCP
purpose: Build, edit, run and debug Power Automate cloud flows from Copilot CLI / VS Code
description: Microsoft's Flow Agent MCP server lets you describe a flow in natural language and have AI create, test and debug Power Automate cloud flows. Reza Dorrani's tutorial shows the full workflow via GitHub Copilot CLI, backed by the power-platform-skills repo.
install_command: copilot mcp add flow-agent (via microsoft/power-platform-skills plugin)
connect_steps: Install the Power Automate skill/plugin from microsoft/power-platform-skills (plugins/power-automate)
Add the remote Flow Agent MCP server in GitHub Copilot CLI (copilot mcp add) or VS Code
Authenticate with your Power Platform environment
Verify: describe a flow (e.g. 'trigger on new response') and let the agent build it
source: youtube:NEW Power Automate Flow Agent MCP Server | Full Tutorial

name: Atlassian Jira MCP (mcp-atlassian)
purpose: Jira and Confluence access: projects, issues, sprints, documents, comments
description: mcp-atlassian exposes Jira Cloud and Confluence tools (list projects, get issues, search tickets, read docs) so agents can work from ticket context instead of guessing. Shown in Amiay Narayan's Jira/Slack/Notion connection tutorial via 'claude mcp add'.
install_command: claude mcp add jira -- npx -y mcp-atlassian
connect_steps: Create an Atlassian API token and note your site URL + email
hermes mcp add jira -- npx -y mcp-atlassian (env: JIRA_URL, JIRA_EMAIL, JIRA_API_TOKEN)
Restart and verify: ask the agent to list projects from your Jira instance
source: youtube:MCP Server and how to connect to them (JIRA, Slack, Notion)

name: Slack MCP
purpose: Post and read Slack messages, list channels and users from an AI agent
description: Official Slack MCP server (@modelcontextprotocol/server-slack) giving agents Slack workspace tools. Used in Amiay Narayan's multi-server tutorial and Brandon Passley's Slack AI-agent-in-Make build.
connect_steps: Create a Slack app/bot and install it to your workspace
hermes mcp add slack -- npx -y @modelcontextprotocol/server-slack (env: SLACK_BOT_TOKEN, SLACK_TEAM_ID)
Restart and verify: ask the agent to list channels and post a test message
source: youtube:MCP Server and how to connect to them (JIRA, Slack, Notion)

name: Notion MCP (official, NotionHQ)
purpose: Full Notion workspace control: pages, databases, search, comments, users
description: Notion's official MCP server (makenotion/notion-mcp-server, npm @notionhq/notion-mcp-server) exposes the whole Notion API to agents. Linked from Zen van Riel's 'AI Second Brain' video and Prompt Circle AI's context-engineering tutorial.
connect_steps: Create a Notion integration at notion.so/my-integrations and copy the token
hermes mcp add notion -- npx @notionhq/notion-mcp-server (env: NOTION_API_KEY)
Share the pages/databases you want accessible with the integration
Restart and verify: ask the agent to search your workspace
source: youtube:Build your AI Second Brain with Notion and Claude (MCP)

name: mcp-notion-server (suekou)
purpose: Lightweight NodeJS Notion MCP server for second-brain / knowledge-base workflows
description: Community NodeJS Notion MCP server run entirely via npx (no code download) with an integration token. The server Zen van Riel used to auto-populate a Notion workspace with Claude.
connect_steps: Create a Notion integration and copy its token
hermes mcp add notion-community -- npx mcp-notion-server (env: NOTION_TOKEN)
Grant the integration access to target pages
Restart and verify: ask the agent to create a page in your workspace
source: youtube:Build your AI Second Brain with Notion and Claude (MCP)

name: MCP Inspector
purpose: Debug, test and inspect MCP servers in a web UI
description: Official MCP Inspector lets you point it at any MCP server (local stdio or remote) to browse tools, resources and prompts and fire test calls. Prompt Circle AI uses it to validate a custom Notion MCP server during development.
connect_steps: Run 'npx @modelcontextprotocol/inspector' to start the web UI
Enter the server command (e.g. npx mcp-notion-server) or remote URL in the inspector
Connect and exercise tools before wiring into Hermes config.yaml
source: youtube:Build a Notion MCP Server: Context Engineering Tutorial

name: FastMCP (Python framework)
purpose: Build custom MCP servers in Python in minutes with decorators
description: FastMCP is the de-facto Python framework for writing MCP servers (tools, resources, prompts via simple decorators, stdio or HTTP). Great Adib's tutorial builds a full SQLite budget app server with it from scratch.
connect_steps: pip install fastmcp (or uvx fastmcp)
Define tools with @mcp.tool() in a server.py, then run it (python server.py)
hermes mcp add my-server -- uvx fastmcp run server.py
Verify with MCP Inspector or a test prompt
source: youtube:Build Custom MCP Servers From Scratch With Fast-MCP | Full Project With SQLite DB for beginners

name: Filesystem MCP
purpose: Read/write local files and directories safely from an agent
description: Official filesystem server (@modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem) exposing file read/write/search tools scoped to allowed directories. Included in Rahul Shetty's agent video alongside browser and DB servers.
connect_steps: hermes mcp add filesystem -- npx -y @modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem C:/Users/HP/xomni
Restrict to the directories the agent may touch
Restart and verify: ask the agent to list files in the allowed directory
source: youtube:Build AI Agent with MCP Servers to Automate - Browser, API, SQL & File Systems

name: Zapier MCP
purpose: Connect AI assistants to 8,000+ apps (Airtable, Gmail, Slack, CRMs) via OAuth
description: Zapier's official MCP lets agents read data, create contacts, send messages and update records across connected apps through one OAuth hub. Zapier's 2026 tutorial shows setup with Claude Desktop using their MCP button and connector prompts.
install_command: hermes mcp add zapier --transport http --url https://mcp.zapier.com (OAuth)
connect_steps: Go to zapier.com/mcp and select the AI assistant (e.g. Claude)
Copy the generated prompt/URL and complete the OAuth flow to authorize apps
Add the remote MCP endpoint to Hermes config.yaml mcp_servers (http transport)
Verify: ask the agent to create a contact or send a message through a connected app
source: youtube:MCP Tutorial: Complete Guide for 2026

name: DuckDuckGo MCP
purpose: Web search via DuckDuckGo from any MCP client
description: DuckDuckGo MCP server (npx duckduckgo-mcp-server) adds web search to agents; offered out of the box in Docker's MCP catalog, which NetworkChuck enables in his Docker MCP tutorial.
connect_steps: hermes mcp add ddg-search -- npx -y duckduckgo-mcp-server
Restart and verify: ask the agent to search the web for a current topic
source: youtube:you need to learn MCP RIGHT NOW!! (Model Context Protocol)

name: Fetch MCP
purpose: Fetch URLs and convert web pages to markdown for LLM consumption
description: Fetch server grabs a URL and returns clean markdown so agents can read docs, articles and APIs. NetworkChuck adds it from Docker's MCP catalog ('Fetch. It'll grab URLs.') in his Docker MCP tutorial.
connect_steps: hermes mcp add fetch -- npx -y @modelcontextprotocol/server-fetch (or enable 'fetch' from the Docker MCP catalog)
Restart and verify: ask the agent to summarize a URL you provide
source: youtube:you need to learn MCP RIGHT NOW!! (Model Context Protocol)

name: CoinGecko MCP
purpose: Live crypto prices and market data from CoinGecko's API
description: CoinGecko MCP server pulls real-time crypto prices, trending coins and market stats for agents. NetworkChuck demonstrates it in Cursor/Claude ('what is the current price of XRP') via the Docker MCP catalog.
connect_steps: hermes mcp add coingecko -- npx -y coingecko-mcp-server
Optional: set COINGECKO_API_KEY env for higher rate limits
Restart and verify: ask the agent for the current price of a coin
source: youtube:you need to learn MCP RIGHT NOW!! (Model Context Protocol)

name: Svelte MCP
purpose: Svelte/SvelteKit documentation and framework knowledge for AI coding assistants
description: Remote Svelte MCP server (@sveltejs/mcp, repo sveltejs/ai-tools) added as an HTTP server in GitHub's Copilot CLI tutorial, letting Copilot consult Svelte docs and inspect SvelteKit apps while coding.
connect_steps: hermes mcp add svelte --transport http --url <svelte mcp endpoint> (or npx @sveltejs/mcp for the CLI version)
Restart and verify: ask the agent Svelte-specific framework questions
source: youtube:How to use MCP servers with GitHub Copilot CLI | Tutorial for beginners

name: ExecuteAutomation Playwright MCP
purpose: Playwright MCP fork with AI-powered selector strategies (XPath, AI locators)
description: ExecuteAutomation's Playwright MCP server (docs at executeautomation.github.io/mcp-playwright) adds AI-driven selector generation on top of Playwright MCP. Linked from the Execute Automation database-server video description.
connect_steps: hermes mcp add ea-playwright -- npx -y executeautomation/mcp-playwright
Optional env: PLAYWRIGHT_AI_* keys for AI locator features
Restart and verify: ask the agent to automate a form and submit it
source: youtube:Database MCP Server: Connect Postgres DB, SQL Server and Sqlite
